name: Reverse walljump: cross a shaft facing back, then wall jump into the far wall
techNote: A 56-wide shaft: a metal wall on the left (face x 100) that ends at y 480 with a spike wall under it, and a metal pillar on the right (face x 156, top y 400, 120 wide) capped with spikes, under a spike ceiling from y 530 over the pillar. The finish box hangs past the pillar's far side. Slide down the left wall holding left, then hold right for exactly 4 ticks and let go: the dot drifts across inside the left wall's wall coyote window (OnWall still on, localScale held at wallCoyoteDir -1, so the sprite keeps facing left) while facingRight turns right with Velocity.x, and once the pillar sits 25-27 u ahead of its centre the rays cast right find it while the front ground ray is still short of it. That cling stores wallCoyoteDir = localScale.x = -1, and as long as the stick stays at rest it holds: the dot slides down the pillar facing away from it, 10 u off its face. Jump 30-33 ticks after letting go and release it 14-16 ticks later: the wall jump goes against localScale, +460 into the pillar and 730 up, rides straight up the face for the 7-tick lock and crosses the spike cap under the ceiling into the box (tick 86). A normal cling on the pillar kicks left into the spike wall; every jump off the left wall (or in its coyote ticks, with any jump cut) starts too high and hits the ceiling or lands on the cap; a fall off the left wall can't cross the 120-wide cap. Hold right 3 ticks (the short demo) and the pillar is never reached in the window; 5 ticks (the long demo) and the front ground ray starts inside the pillar: grounded on its face, the jump is an 805 ground jump that hits the ceiling.

ghosts.label: Right 3 ticks: normal cling, kicks left
Right 5 ticks: grounded on the face, ground jump
